prompt: Square refined detailed painterly mythology encyclopedia illustration of MANOHARA, kinnari bird-woman heroine, in the traditional human-upper / BIRD-LOWER KINNARI anatomical form. One graceful adult female celestial creature with human head, neck, shoulders and exactly TWO human arms, modest close-fitting ancient Southeast Asian red-and-gold brocade bodice ending at WAIST. Below waist the body is unmistakably FEATHERED BIRD anatomy: rounded feathered avian haunches, exactly TWO avian WINGS growing from bird-body sides at waist/hips and gently spread, exactly TWO long SCALY BIRD LEGS ending in two clearly visible three-forward-toed taloned BIRD FEET, one flowing feathered tail behind. NO human legs or human feet, no skirt disguising feathered lower body, no detachable costume wings. Full coherent hybrid from head through both wing tips, tail and bird feet entirely in frame, all essential anatomy legible. Graceful poised dance stance at still lotus-lined mountain lake, royal celestial dignity with romantic longing and freedom, peaceful refined feminine expression, no captivity violence. Premium painterly realism with rich walnut shadows, restrained gold feather/costume glints and forest-green landscape, elegant muted bronze-brown feather textures. No ordinary woman wearing feathers, no extra arms, horns, animal head, halo, weapons, text, borders or watermark. Contemporary artistic interpretation of Manohara as kinnari; this is not a reconstruction of the separate entirely human Borobudur relief portrayal.

visual_review.notes: Individually viewed full figure: one woman upper body with two arms seamlessly joined at waist to unmistakable feathered bird haunches, two wings, one long feathered tail and exactly two scaly bird legs/taloned feet. No human legs or cloth hiding bird anatomy; both bird feet and wing tips are legible. Gracious dancing posture and gentle lakeside expression preserve celestial romantic heroine aura. Museum primary source supports kinnari bird-lower-body form, explicitly distinguished from Borobudur's fully human Manohara depiction. No horns, animal head, extra arms, text or watermark.
